98	def _assert(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
99	    """Every structural interpreter failure surfaces as AssertionError."""
100	    if not condition:
101	        raise AssertionError(message)
102	
103	
104	class _Interpreter:
105	    """Execute a lowered :class:`Module` of either SSA flavor.
106	
107	    A run returns ``(return_value, trace)`` where ``trace`` records, in
108	    occurrence order, one ``(function_name, (positional arguments))`` tuple
109	    per executed :class:`Call` instruction (including recursive and
110	    cross-function calls).  A void entry returns ``None``.
111	    """
112	
113	    def __init__(self, module: Module):
114	        _assert(isinstance(module, Module),
115	                f"interpreter expects a Module, got {type(module).__name__}")
116	        self.ssa = bool(module.ssa)
117	        self._functions = {fn_.name: fn_ for fn_ in module.functions}
118	
119	    def run(self, entry: str, arguments):
120	        fn_ = self._functions.get(entry)
121	        _assert(fn_ is not None, f"unknown entry function {entry!r}")
122	        arguments = tuple(arguments)
123	        _assert(
124	            len(arguments) == len(fn_.params),
125	            f"entry {entry!r} expects {len(fn_.params)} argument(s), "
126	            f"got {len(arguments)}",
127	        )
128	        trace: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
129	        value = self._invoke(fn_, arguments, trace)
130	        return value, trace
131	
132	    # -- one function activation -------------------------------------------
133	
134	    def _invoke(self, fn_, arguments, trace: list):
135	        # SSA: unique Temp definitions; non-SSA: mutable Slots plus Temps
136	        # (the short-circuit result temporary is written once per executed
137	        # path, so ordinary overwrite semantics suffice).
138	        definitions: dict[int, object] = {}
139	        slots: dict[int, object] = {}
140	        temps: dict[int, object] = {}
141	
142	        for parameter, argument in zip(fn_.params, arguments):
143	            if self.ssa:
144	                _assert(parameter.temp is not None,
145	                        f"SSA parameter {parameter.name!r} has no definition")
146	                definitions[id(parameter.temp)] = argument
147	            else:
148	                slots[parameter.slot.id] = argument
149	
150	        def write(ref, value) -> None:
151	            if self.ssa:
152	                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp) and not isinstance(ref, Slot),
153	                        f"{fn_.name}: non-Temp definition {ref!r} in SSA IR")
154	                definitions[id(ref)] = value
155	            elif isinstance(ref, Slot):
156	                slots[ref.id] = value
157	            else:
158	                temps[id(ref)] = value
159	
160	        def read(ref):
161	            if self.ssa:
162	                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp),
163	                        f"{fn_.name}: SSA read of non-Temp value {ref!r}")
164	                _assert(id(ref) in definitions,
165	                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined SSA value {ref}")
166	                return definitions[id(ref)]
167	            if isinstance(ref, Slot):
168	                _assert(ref.id in slots,
169	                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined slot {ref}")
170	                return slots[ref.id]
171	            _assert(id(ref) in temps,
172	                    f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined temporary {ref}")
173	            return temps[id(ref)]
174	
175	        def execute(instruction) -> None:
176	            if isinstance(instruction, Const):
177	                write(instruction.dest, instruction.value)
178	            elif isinstance(instruction, Copy):
179	                write(instruction.dest, read(instruction.src))
180	            elif isinstance(instruction, BinOp):
181	                left = read(instruction.left)
182	                right = read(instruction.right)
183	                write(instruction.dest,
184	                      _apply_binop(instruction, left, right, fn_.name))
185	            elif isinstance(instruction, Call):
186	                callee = self._functions.get(instruction.name)
187	                _assert(callee is not None,
188	                        f"{fn_.name}: call to unknown function "
189	                        f"{instruction.name!r}")
190	                values = tuple(read(operand) for operand in instruction.args)
191	                _assert(
192	                    len(values) == len(callee.params),
193	                    f"call to {instruction.name!r}: arity mismatch at run "
194	                    f"time ({len(values)} for {len(callee.params)})",
195	                )
196	                # Log at the moment the call happens, before the callee's
197	                # own calls, so the trace follows evaluation order.
198	                trace.append((instruction.name, values))
199	                write(instruction.dest,
200	                      self._invoke(callee, values, trace))
201	            else:
202	                _assert(False,
203	                        f"{fn_.name}: unknown instruction {instruction!r}")
204	
205	        known_blocks = {id(block) for block in fn_.blocks}
206	        block = fn_.entry
207	        previous = None
208	        steps_left = _STEP_LIMIT
209	
210	        while True:
211	            _assert(steps_left > 0,
212	                    f"{fn_.name}: step budget exhausted "
213	                    "(program does not terminate?)")
214	            steps_left -= 1
215	
216	            if self.ssa:
217	                # All incoming values are read off the *actual* predecessor
218	                # edge before any phi result is bound, matching phi
219	                # semantics when header phis reference one another.
220	                pending: list[tuple[Temp, object]] = []
221	                for phi in block.phis:
222	                    _assert(previous is not None,
223	                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi in entry block "
224	                            "has no predecessor edge")
225	                    source = phi.entries.get(previous)
226	                    _assert(source is not None,
227	                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi {phi.dest} has "
228	                            f"no incoming value from predecessor "
229	                            f"{previous.label}")
230	                    pending.append((phi.dest, read(source)))
231	                for destination, value in pending:
232	                    definitions[id(destination)] = value
233	            else:
234	                _assert(not block.phis,
235	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi node in non-SSA IR")
236	
237	            for instruction in block.instructions:
238	                execute(instruction)
239	
240	            terminator = block.terminator
241	            _assert(terminator is not None,
242	                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: missing terminator")
243	
244	            if isinstance(terminator, Return):
245	                if terminator.value is None:
246	                    return None
247	                return read(terminator.value)
248	
249	            if isinstance(terminator, Jump):
250	                _assert(id(terminator.target) in known_blocks,
251	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: jump to unknown block "
252	                        f"{terminator.target.label}")
253	                previous, block = block, terminator.target
254	                continue
255	
256	            if isinstance(terminator, Branch):
257	                condition = read(terminator.cond)
258	                _assert(isinstance(condition, bool),
259	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch on non-bool "
260	                        f"value {condition!r}")
261	                target = (terminator.true_target if condition
262	                          else terminator.false_target)
263	                _assert(id(target) in known_blocks,
264	                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
265	                        f"{target.label}")
266	                previous, block = block, target
267	                continue
268	
269	            _assert(False,
270	                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: unknown terminator "
271	                    f"{terminator!r}")

"""Semantic-equivalence tests for the non-SSA -> pruned SSA conversion.

The existing tests compare node structure and rendered text.  This module
instead *executes* both flavors of IR and proves that, for one and the same
lowered program, :func:`to_ssa` preserves observable behavior:

* the entry function is invoked with fixed, concrete arguments;
* the non-SSA :class:`Module` returned by ``lower_module`` and the new SSA
  :class:`Module` returned by ``to_ssa`` are each interpreted independently;
* the return value and the ordered trace of function calls
  ``(callee name, positional argument tuple)`` must be identical.

The interpreter is deliberately small and works over both IR flavors:

* non-SSA state is a mutable slot file (parameters / ``let`` variables) plus
  temporary storage, so the multi-written result temporary of a
  short-circuit operation simply holds whichever write the executed path
  performed;
* SSA state is a map of unique :class:`Temp` definitions.  Phi inputs are
  chosen from the block *actually arrived from*, so a loop header reads its
  entry values on the first visit and the current round's values on every
  back edge.

Calls that did not happen (untaken ``if`` branches, unevaluated right
operands of short-circuit ``and``/``or``, zero-trip loops) therefore never
appear in the trace.

Everything here is deterministic and standard-library-only; the only
supported pipeline input is the public dict/list AST (the same subset the
README documents, with int/bool/void and add/sub/mul arithmetic).  Any
interpreter failure -- a missing block target or terminator, a phi without
an entry for the actual predecessor, or a read of an undefined value --
raises ``AssertionError``; a case is never skipped.
"""
import json
import unittest

from compiler_ir import (
    BinOp,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
    lower_module,
    to_ssa,
)

from test_pipeline import (
    arith,
    assign,
    block,
    bool_,
    call,
    compare,
    func,
    if_,
    int_,
    let,
    logical,
    param,
    program,
    ret,
    var,
    while_,
)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IR interpreter (shared by the non-SSA and SSA modules)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Every lowered program in this file is tiny and terminates quickly; this is
# only a belt-and-braces guard against an accidentally non-terminating case.
_STEP_LIMIT = 100_000

_ARITH = {
    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
}

_COMPARE = {
    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


def _assert(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    """Every structural interpreter failure surfaces as AssertionError."""
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)


class _Interpreter:
    """Execute a lowered :class:`Module` of either SSA flavor.

    A run returns ``(return_value, trace)`` where ``trace`` records, in
    occurrence order, one ``(function_name, (positional arguments))`` tuple
    per executed :class:`Call` instruction (including recursive and
    cross-function calls).  A void entry returns ``None``.
    """

    def __init__(self, module: Module):
        _assert(isinstance(module, Module),
                f"interpreter expects a Module, got {type(module).__name__}")
        self.ssa = bool(module.ssa)
        self._functions = {fn_.name: fn_ for fn_ in module.functions}

    def run(self, entry: str, arguments):
        fn_ = self._functions.get(entry)
        _assert(fn_ is not None, f"unknown entry function {entry!r}")
        arguments = tuple(arguments)
        _assert(
            len(arguments) == len(fn_.params),
            f"entry {entry!r} expects {len(fn_.params)} argument(s), "
            f"got {len(arguments)}",
        )
        trace: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
        value = self._invoke(fn_, arguments, trace)
        return value, trace

    # -- one function activation -------------------------------------------

    def _invoke(self, fn_, arguments, trace: list):
        # SSA: unique Temp definitions; non-SSA: mutable Slots plus Temps
        # (the short-circuit result temporary is written once per executed
        # path, so ordinary overwrite semantics suffice).
        definitions: dict[int, object] = {}
        slots: dict[int, object] = {}
        temps: dict[int, object] = {}

        for parameter, argument in zip(fn_.params, arguments):
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(parameter.temp is not None,
                        f"SSA parameter {parameter.name!r} has no definition")
                definitions[id(parameter.temp)] = argument
            else:
                slots[parameter.slot.id] = argument

        def write(ref, value) -> None:
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp) and not isinstance(ref, Slot),
                        f"{fn_.name}: non-Temp definition {ref!r} in SSA IR")
                definitions[id(ref)] = value
            elif isinstance(ref, Slot):
                slots[ref.id] = value
            else:
                temps[id(ref)] = value

        def read(ref):
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp),
                        f"{fn_.name}: SSA read of non-Temp value {ref!r}")
                _assert(id(ref) in definitions,
                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined SSA value {ref}")
                return definitions[id(ref)]
            if isinstance(ref, Slot):
                _assert(ref.id in slots,
                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined slot {ref}")
                return slots[ref.id]
            _assert(id(ref) in temps,
                    f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined temporary {ref}")
            return temps[id(ref)]

        def execute(instruction) -> None:
            if isinstance(instruction, Const):
                write(instruction.dest, instruction.value)
            elif isinstance(instruction, Copy):
                write(instruction.dest, read(instruction.src))
            elif isinstance(instruction, BinOp):
                left = read(instruction.left)
                right = read(instruction.right)
                write(instruction.dest,
                      _apply_binop(instruction, left, right, fn_.name))
            elif isinstance(instruction, Call):
                callee = self._functions.get(instruction.name)
                _assert(callee is not None,
                        f"{fn_.name}: call to unknown function "
                        f"{instruction.name!r}")
                values = tuple(read(operand) for operand in instruction.args)
                _assert(
                    len(values) == len(callee.params),
                    f"call to {instruction.name!r}: arity mismatch at run "
                    f"time ({len(values)} for {len(callee.params)})",
                )
                # Log at the moment the call happens, before the callee's
                # own calls, so the trace follows evaluation order.
                trace.append((instruction.name, values))
                write(instruction.dest,
                      self._invoke(callee, values, trace))
            else:
                _assert(False,
                        f"{fn_.name}: unknown instruction {instruction!r}")

        known_blocks = {id(block) for block in fn_.blocks}
        block = fn_.entry
        previous = None
        steps_left = _STEP_LIMIT

        while True:
            _assert(steps_left > 0,
                    f"{fn_.name}: step budget exhausted "
                    "(program does not terminate?)")
            steps_left -= 1

            if self.ssa:
                # All incoming values are read off the *actual* predecessor
                # edge before any phi result is bound, matching phi
                # semantics when header phis reference one another.
                pending: list[tuple[Temp, object]] = []
                for phi in block.phis:
                    _assert(previous is not None,
                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi in entry block "
                            "has no predecessor edge")
                    source = phi.entries.get(previous)
                    _assert(source is not None,
                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi {phi.dest} has "
                            f"no incoming value from predecessor "
                            f"{previous.label}")
                    pending.append((phi.dest, read(source)))
                for destination, value in pending:
                    definitions[id(destination)] = value
            else:
                _assert(not block.phis,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi node in non-SSA IR")

            for instruction in block.instructions:
                execute(instruction)

            terminator = block.terminator
            _assert(terminator is not None,
                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: missing terminator")

            if isinstance(terminator, Return):
                if terminator.value is None:
                    return None
                return read(terminator.value)

            if isinstance(terminator, Jump):
                _assert(id(terminator.target) in known_blocks,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: jump to unknown block "
                        f"{terminator.target.label}")
                previous, block = block, terminator.target
                continue

            if isinstance(terminator, Branch):
                condition = read(terminator.cond)
                _assert(isinstance(condition, bool),
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch on non-bool "
                        f"value {condition!r}")
                target = (terminator.true_target if condition
                          else terminator.false_target)
                _assert(id(target) in known_blocks,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
                        f"{target.label}")
                previous, block = block, target
                continue

            _assert(False,
                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: unknown terminator "
                    f"{terminator!r}")


def _apply_binop(instruction: BinOp, left, right, fn_name: str):
    if instruction.kind == "arith":
        # The type checker guarantees plain ints; reject bools explicitly so
        # Python's bool/int overlap cannot hide a lowering mix-up.
        _assert(type(left) is int and type(right) is int,
                f"{fn_name}: arithmetic {instruction.operator!r} on "
                f"non-int operands {left!r}, {right!r}")
        operation = _ARITH.get(instruction.operator)
        _assert(operation is not None,
                f"{fn_name}: unsupported arithmetic operator "
                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
        return operation(left, right)

    if instruction.kind == "compare":
        _assert(type(left) == type(right),
                f"{fn_name}: comparison {instruction.operator!r} between "
                f"mismatched value types {left!r}, {right!r}")
        operation = _COMPARE.get(instruction.operator)
        _assert(operation is not None,
                f"{fn_name}: unsupported comparison operator "
                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
        return operation(left, right)

    _assert(False, f"{fn_name}: unknown BinOp kind {instruction.kind!r}")

        f"arguments {arguments!r}\n"
        f"reproducible AST:\n"
        f"{json.dumps(ast, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)}\n"
        f"non-SSA result (return value, call trace): {non_ssa_result!r}\n"
        f"SSA     result (return value, call trace): {ssa_result!r}"
    )

                    ssa_result = _interpret(ssa_module, entry, arguments)

                        non_ssa_result, ssa_result,
                        msg=_failure_message(
                            name, ast, entry, arguments,
                            non_ssa_result, ssa_result),
                    )

                    # necessary but not sufficient, so anchor the observable
                    # result independently.
                    self.assertEqual(

1	"""Dead-code elimination on pruned SSA form.
2	
3	The entry point :func:`eliminate_dead_code` takes an SSA :class:`Module`
4	produced by :func:`~compiler_ir.ssa.to_ssa` and returns a brand new SSA
5	:class:`Module` with unreachable definitions removed; the input module is
6	never mutated and shares no mutable function, block, instruction or phi
7	container with the result.
8	
9	Liveness is traced per function, definition-to-use, from fixed roots:
10	
11	* every operand of a ``Return`` or ``Branch`` terminator;
12	* every ``Call`` instruction, regardless of whether its result is used --
13	  the call itself and its position in the instruction stream are observable
14	  behavior -- together with all of its argument definitions.
15	
16	A ``Const``, ``BinOp`` or ``Phi`` that cannot reach one of those roots is
17	deleted.  The trace runs on the whole function at once, so chains feeding
18	only other dead definitions and closed phi cycles die together in one pass;
19	elimination is then repeated until no new dead definition appears.
20	
21	The pass is purely subtractive.  No constants are folded, branches
22	rewritten, blocks deleted or control flow reordered.  Function order,
23	signatures, parameters, return types, block labels and order, terminators,
24	the relative order of surviving instructions and the predecessor order of
25	surviving phis are all preserved, and SSA numbers of surviving values are
26	left untouched (the output may therefore contain numbering holes).
27	
28	Applying the pass to an already minimal module returns an independent,
29	structurally and textually equivalent copy, so a second
30	:func:`eliminate_dead_code` changes nothing.  A non-:class:`Module` object
31	raises :class:`TypeError`; a non-SSA :class:`Module` raises
32	:class:`ValueError`.
33	"""
34	from .ir_nodes import (
35	    BinOp,
36	    Block,
37	    Branch,
38	    Call,
39	    Const,
40	    Copy,
41	    Function,
42	    Jump,
43	    Module,
44	    Parameter,
45	    Phi,
46	    Return,
47	    Temp,
48	)
49	
50	
51	def eliminate_dead_code(module: Module) -> Module:
52	    """Return a new SSA :class:`Module` with dead definitions removed.
53	
54	    The input module is left untouched; the result shares no mutable
55	    function, block, instruction or phi object with it.
56	
57	    :raises TypeError: if ``module`` is not a :class:`Module` instance.
58	    :raises ValueError: if ``module`` is not in SSA form.
59	    """
60	    if not isinstance(module, Module):
61	        raise TypeError(
62	            "eliminate_dead_code expects a Module, got "
63	            f"{type(module).__name__}"
64	        )
65	    if not getattr(module, "ssa", False):
66	        raise ValueError("eliminate_dead_code expects an SSA Module")
67	    return Module(
68	        [_eliminate_in_function(func) for func in module.functions], ssa=True
69	    )
70	
71	
72	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	# Operand helpers (mirror the ones used by the SSA conversion)
74	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
75	
76	
77	def _operands(ins):
78	    if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
79	        return [ins.left, ins.right]
80	    if isinstance(ins, Call):
81	        return list(ins.args)
82	    # Const has no operands; a Copy cannot survive the non-SSA -> SSA
83	    # conversion (it folds into renaming) but is treated as pure anyway.
84	    if isinstance(ins, Copy):
85	        return [ins.src]
86	    return []
87	
88	
89	def _term_operands(term):
90	    if isinstance(term, Return) and term.value is not None:
91	        return [term.value]
92	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
93	        return [term.cond]
94	    return []
95	
96	
97	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	# Per-function elimination
99	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	
101	
102	def _live_definitions(func: Function) -> set:
103	    """Return the ids of values live from the terminator/call roots.
104	
105	    Roots are every value read by a ``Return`` or ``Branch`` and *every*
106	    ``Call`` instruction (plus, transitively, its arguments): a call whose
107	    result is unused is still observable.  From each root the use-def graph
108	    -- instruction operands and phi incoming values -- is walked to a
109	    fixpoint, so a value only reachable from dead code or a closed phi
110	    cycle is absent from the result.
111	    """
112	    phi_by_dest: dict = {}
113	    operands_by_dest: dict = {}
114	    worklist: list = []
115	
116	    for block in func.blocks:
117	        for ins in block.instructions:
118	            operands_by_dest[id(ins.dest)] = _operands(ins)
119	            if isinstance(ins, Call):
120	                # The call itself is a root even if its result is unused:
121	                # reaching its dest below also pulls in its arguments.
122	                worklist.append(ins.dest)
123	        worklist.extend(_term_operands(block.terminator))
124	        for phi in block.phis:
125	            phi_by_dest[id(phi.dest)] = phi
126	
127	    live: set = set()
128	    while worklist:
129	        value = worklist.pop()
130	        if value is None or id(value) in live:
131	            continue
132	        live.add(id(value))
133	        phi = phi_by_dest.get(id(value))
134	        if phi is not None:
135	            worklist.extend(phi.entries.values())
136	        else:
137	            worklist.extend(operands_by_dest.get(id(value), ()))
138	    return live
139	
140	
141	def _eliminate_in_function(func: Function) -> Function:
142	    live = _live_definitions(func)
143	
144	    new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in func.blocks]
145	    block_map = dict(zip(func.blocks, new_blocks))
146	
147	    # Pre-create one fresh Temp for every surviving definition before
148	    # cloning anything: a phi in an earlier block (e.g. a loop header's
149	    # backedge entry) can reference an instruction defined in a later
150	    # block, and every retained use must resolve to the very same output
151	    # object.  Original ids are kept, so numbering holes from removed
152	    # definitions remain.
153	    value_map: dict = {
154	        id(param.temp): Temp(param.temp.id, param.temp.type)
155	        for param in func.params
156	    }
157	    for block in func.blocks:
158	        for phi in block.phis:
159	            if id(phi.dest) in live:
160	                value_map[id(phi.dest)] = Temp(phi.dest.id, phi.dest.type)
161	        for ins in block.instructions:
162	            if isinstance(ins, Call) or id(ins.dest) in live:
163	                value_map[id(ins.dest)] = Temp(
164	                    ins.dest.id, ins.dest.type
165	                )
166	
167	    def map_value(value):
168	        if value is None:
169	            return None
170	        mapped = value_map.get(id(value))
171	        if mapped is None:
172	            # Defensive: a referenced value with no surviving definition.
173	            # Never occurs for SSA IR produced by to_ssa, where every
174	            # operand of a live construct is itself live.
175	            mapped = Temp(value.id, value.type)
176	            value_map[id(value)] = mapped
177	        return mapped
178	
179	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
180	        for phi in block.phis:
181	            if id(phi.dest) not in live:
182	                continue
183	            entries = {
184	                block_map[pred]: map_value(value)
185	                for pred, value in sorted(
186	                    phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
187	                )
188	            }
189	            new_block.phis.append(Phi(map_value(phi.dest), entries))
190	
191	        for ins in block.instructions:
192	            if not isinstance(ins, Call) and id(ins.dest) not in live:
193	                continue
194	            dest = map_value(ins.dest)
195	            if isinstance(ins, Const):
196	                clone = Const(dest, ins.value)
197	            elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
198	                clone = Copy(dest, map_value(ins.src))
199	            elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
200	                clone = BinOp(
201	                    dest, ins.operator, map_value(ins.left),
202	                    map_value(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
203	                )
204	            else:
205	                clone = Call(
206	                    dest, ins.name,
207	                    [map_value(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
208	                )
209	            new_block.instructions.append(clone)
210	
211	        term = block.terminator
212	        if isinstance(term, Return):
213	            new_block.terminator = Return(map_value(term.value))
214	        elif isinstance(term, Jump):
215	            new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
216	        elif isinstance(term, Branch):
217	            new_block.terminator = Branch(
218	                map_value(term.cond),
219	                block_map[term.true_target],
220	                block_map[term.false_target],
221	            )
222	
223	    new_params = [
224	        Parameter(
225	            param.name,
226	            param.slot,
227	            map_value(param.temp),
228	        )
229	        for param in func.params
230	    ]
231	
232	    return Function(
233	        func.name,
234	        new_params,
235	        func.ret_type,
236	        list(func.locals),
237	        new_blocks,
238	        block_map[func.entry],
239	        ssa=True,
240	    )
241

1	"""The control-flow IR object model.
2	
3	The IR is intentionally tiny and directly traversable::
4	
5	    Module
6	      Function            (signature, local slots, basic blocks)
7	        Block             (phi nodes, ordered instructions, one terminator)
8	          Phi             (SSA only; one incoming value per predecessor)
9	          Instruction     (Const / Copy / BinOp / Call, all write a dest)
10	          Terminator      (Return / Jump / Branch)
11	
12	Two flavors of module exist:
13	
14	* non-SSA (produced by :func:`lower_module`): value references are
15	  :class:`Temp` -- numbered temporaries produced by instructions -- and
16	  :class:`Slot`, numbered mutable local storage (parameters and ``let``
17	  variables).  Temporaries are mostly single assignment; the sole exception
18	  is the result temporary of a short-circuit boolean operation, which is
19	  written once on each participating path, as is natural in non-SSA form.
20	* SSA (produced by :func:`to_ssa`): every parameter and every instruction
21	  result is a unique definition, slots never appear, and control-flow joins
22	  carry :class:`Phi` nodes listed before the block's ordinary instructions.
23	
24	Both flavors reuse the same node classes; a module's ``ssa`` flag (and each
25	function's) says which one it is.
26	"""
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
30	from typing import Optional, Union
31	
32	
33	@dataclass(frozen=True)
34	class Temp:
35	    id: int
36	    type: str
37	
38	    def __str__(self) -> str:
39	        return f"%t{self.id}"
40	
41	
42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class Slot:
44	    """A mutable local slot (parameter or ``let`` variable)."""
45	
46	    id: int
47	    type: str
48	
49	    def __str__(self) -> str:
50	        return f"%v{self.id}"
51	
52	
53	ValueRef = Union[Temp, Slot]
54	
55	
56	@dataclass
57	class Const:
58	    dest: Temp
59	    value: Union[int, bool]
60	
61	    @property
62	    def op(self) -> str:
63	        return "const"
64	
65	
66	@dataclass
67	class Copy:
68	    dest: Union[Temp, Slot]
69	    src: ValueRef
70	
71	    @property
72	    def op(self) -> str:
73	        return "copy"
74	
75	
76	@dataclass
77	class BinOp:
78	    dest: Temp
79	    operator: str
80	    left: ValueRef
81	    right: ValueRef
82	    kind: str  # "arith" or "compare"
83	    type: str  # result type
84	
85	    @property
86	    def op(self) -> str:
87	        return self.kind
88	
89	
90	@dataclass
91	class Call:
92	    dest: Temp
93	    name: str
94	    args: list[ValueRef]
95	    type: str
96	
97	    @property
98	    def op(self) -> str:
99	        return "call"
100	
101	
102	Instruction = Union[Const, Copy, BinOp, Call]
103	
104	
105	@dataclass(eq=False)
106	class Phi:
107	    """An SSA phi function: merges definitions from predecessor blocks.
108	
109	    ``entries`` maps a predecessor :class:`Block` to the value that is live
110	    on that edge.  Entries are kept sorted by predecessor label whenever a
111	    module is emitted by :func:`to_ssa`; only reachable predecessors occur.
112	    """
113	
114	    dest: Temp
115	    entries: dict["Block", ValueRef] = field(default_factory=dict)
116	
117	    @property
118	    def op(self) -> str:
119	        return "phi"
120	
121	    @property
122	    def type(self) -> str:
123	        return self.dest.type
124	
125	
126	@dataclass
127	class Return:
128	    value: Optional[ValueRef]
129	
130	    @property
131	    def op(self) -> str:
132	        return "return"
133	
134	
135	@dataclass
136	class Jump:
137	    target: "Block"
138	
139	    @property
140	    def op(self) -> str:
141	        return "jump"
142	
143	
144	@dataclass
145	class Branch:
146	    cond: ValueRef
147	    true_target: "Block"
148	    false_target: "Block"
149	
150	    @property
151	    def op(self) -> str:
152	        return "br"
153	
154	
155	Terminator = Union[Return, Jump, Branch]
156	
157	
158	@dataclass(eq=False)
159	class Block:
160	    id: int
161	    instructions: list[Instruction] = field(default_factory=list)
162	    terminator: Optional[Terminator] = None
163	    # SSA only; empty in non-SSA blocks.  Phi nodes precede the ordinary
164	    # instructions.
165	    phis: list[Phi] = field(default_factory=list)
166	
167	    @property
168	    def label(self) -> str:
169	        return f"b{self.id}"
170	
171	    @property
172	    def is_terminated(self) -> bool:
173	        return self.terminator is not None
174	
175	
176	@dataclass
177	class Parameter:
178	    name: str
179	    slot: Slot
180	    # SSA only: the unique parameter definition.  None in non-SSA functions,
181	    # where the parameter is read through ``slot``.
182	    temp: Optional[Temp] = None
183	
184	
185	@dataclass
186	class Function:
187	    name: str
188	    params: list[Parameter]
189	    ret_type: str
190	    locals: list[Slot]
191	    blocks: list[Block]
192	    entry: Block
193	    ssa: bool = False
194	
195	    def is_void(self) -> bool:
196	        return self.ret_type == "void"
197	
198	
199	@dataclass
200	class Module:
201	    functions: list[Function]
202	    ssa: bool = False
203

1	"""Deterministic plain-text rendering of the IR.
2	
3	The output is a direct, fixed-order walk of the IR tree: functions in
4	module order, blocks in id order, phi nodes (SSA only) then instructions in
5	emission order.  Nothing is sorted by name or derived from object identity
6	-- phi entries are ordered by predecessor label, which is itself fixed -- so
7	a given module renders byte-identically across processes and repeated
8	conversions.
9	
10	Non-SSA modules render exactly as before (``%tN`` temporaries, ``%vN``
11	slots).  SSA modules use a distinct representation: every value is a unique
12	``%N`` definition, parameters are rendered with their SSA value, no locals
13	section is emitted, and phi lines carry the result type plus one
14	``[block, value]`` pair per reachable predecessor.
15	"""
16	from .ir_nodes import (
17	    BinOp,
18	    Branch,
19	    Call,
20	    Const,
21	    Copy,
22	    Function,
23	    Jump,
24	    Module,
25	    Phi,
26	    Return,
27	)
28	
29	
30	def _render_instruction(ins, value) -> str:
31	    if isinstance(ins, Const):
32	        literal = "true" if ins.value is True else "false" if ins.value is False else str(ins.value)
33	        return f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.dest.type} = const {literal}"
34	    if isinstance(ins, Copy):
35	        return f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.dest.type} = copy {value(ins.src)}"
36	    if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
37	        return (
38	            f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.type} = {ins.kind} {ins.operator} "
39	            f"{value(ins.left)} {value(ins.right)}"
40	        )
41	    if isinstance(ins, Call):
42	        args = ", ".join(value(a) for a in ins.args)
43	        return f"    {value(ins.dest)}: {ins.type} = call {ins.name}({args})"
44	    raise AssertionError(f"unknown instruction: {ins!r}")  # pragma: no cover
45	
46	
47	def _render_phi(phi: Phi, value) -> str:
48	    sources = ", ".join(
49	        f"[{block.label}, {value(val)}]"
50	        for block, val in sorted(phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id)
51	    )
52	    return f"    {value(phi.dest)}: {phi.type} = phi {sources}"
53	
54	
55	def _render_terminator(term, value) -> str:
56	    if isinstance(term, Return):
57	        if term.value is None:
58	            return "    return"
59	        return f"    return {value(term.value)}"
60	    if isinstance(term, Jump):
61	        return f"    jump {term.target.label}"
62	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
63	        return (
64	            f"    br {value(term.cond)}, {term.true_target.label}, "
65	            f"{term.false_target.label}"
66	        )
67	    raise AssertionError(f"unknown terminator: {term!r}")  # pragma: no cover
68	
69	
70	def _render_function(func: Function) -> str:
71	    ssa = getattr(func, "ssa", False)
72	
73	    if ssa:
74	        def value(v) -> str:
75	            return f"%{v.id}"
76	
77	        params = ", ".join(
78	            f"{p.name}: {p.temp.type} @ {value(p.temp)}" for p in func.params
79	        )
80	    else:
81	        def value(v) -> str:
82	            return str(v)
83	
84	        params = ", ".join(f"{p.name}: {p.slot.type} @ {value(p.slot)}"
85	                           for p in func.params)
86	
87	    lines = [f"function {func.name}({params}) -> {func.ret_type} {{"]
88	    if not ssa and func.locals:
89	        lines.append("  locals:")
90	        for slot in func.locals:
91	            lines.append(f"    {value(slot)}: {slot.type}")
92	    for block in func.blocks:
93	        lines.append(f"  {block.label}:")
94	        if ssa:
95	            for phi in block.phis:
96	                lines.append(_render_phi(phi, value))
97	        for ins in block.instructions:
98	            lines.append(_render_instruction(ins, value))
99	        lines.append(_render_terminator(block.terminator, value))
100	    lines.append("}")
101	    return "\n".join(lines)
102	
103	
104	def render_module(module: Module) -> str:
105	    """Render a :class:`Module` to deterministic plain text."""
106	    parts = ["module"]
107	    parts.extend(_render_function(func) for func in module.functions)
108	    return "\n".join(parts) + "\n"

1	"""Lowering from the validated, semantically checked AST to non-SSA IR.
2	
3	Numbering is fully deterministic: functions are processed in AST order and
4	each function numbers blocks and temporaries from zero, allocating them in
5	the depth-first order in which statements and expressions are visited.
6	No dictionary key order, object identity or set iteration influences the
7	result, so the same AST produces byte-identical IR in every process.
8	
9	Control flow
10	------------
11	* Every function gets an entry block ``b0``; parameters occupy the first
12	  local slots.
13	* ``if`` emits a conditional branch to true/false blocks and creates a
14	  merge block only when at least one branch can actually reach it; an
15	  unreachable, empty merge is never left behind.
16	* ``while`` emits a condition block, body block and exit block.
17	* ``return`` terminates its path; statements following a terminator on the
18	  same path produce no IR.
19	* Short-circuit ``and``/``or`` lower to control flow; the right operand is
20	  only evaluated on the path that needs it.
21	"""
22	from typing import Optional
23	
24	from .ast_validate import validate_program
25	from .ir_nodes import (
26	    BinOp,
27	    Block,
28	    Branch,
29	    Call,
30	    Const,
31	    Copy,
32	    Function,
33	    Jump,
34	    Module,
35	    Parameter,
36	    Return,
37	    Slot,
38	    Temp,
39	)
40	from .semantics import analyze
41	
42	INT = "int"
43	BOOL = "bool"
44	
45	
46	class _Scope:
47	    __slots__ = ("parent", "names")
48	
49	    def __init__(self, parent: Optional["_Scope"] = None):
50	        self.parent = parent
51	        self.names: dict[str, Slot] = {}
52	
53	    def declare(self, name: str, slot: Slot) -> None:
54	        self.names[name] = slot
55	
56	    def lookup(self, name: str) -> Optional[Slot]:
57	        scope: Optional[_Scope] = self
58	        while scope is not None:
59	            if name in scope.names:
60	                return scope.names[name]
61	            scope = scope.parent
62	        return None

65	class _Lowerer:
66	    def __init__(self, ast: dict, callee_types: dict[str, str]):
67	        self.ast = ast
68	        self.callee_types = callee_types
69	        self.functions: list[Function] = []

"""Lowering from the validated, semantically checked AST to non-SSA IR.

Numbering is fully deterministic: functions are processed in AST order and
each function numbers blocks and temporaries from zero, allocating them in
the depth-first order in which statements and expressions are visited.
No dictionary key order, object identity or set iteration influences the
result, so the same AST produces byte-identical IR in every process.

Control flow
------------
* Every function gets an entry block ``b0``; parameters occupy the first
  local slots.
* ``if`` emits a conditional branch to true/false blocks and creates a
  merge block only when at least one branch can actually reach it; an
  unreachable, empty merge is never left behind.
* ``while`` emits a condition block, body block and exit block.
* ``return`` terminates its path; statements following a terminator on the
  same path produce no IR.
* Short-circuit ``and``/``or`` lower to control flow; the right operand is
  only evaluated on the path that needs it.
"""
from typing import Optional

from .ast_validate import validate_program
from .ir_nodes import (
    BinOp,
    Block,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Function,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Parameter,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
)
from .semantics import analyze

INT = "int"
BOOL = "bool"


class _Scope:
    __slots__ = ("parent", "names")

    def __init__(self, parent: Optional["_Scope"] = None):
        self.parent = parent
        self.names: dict[str, Slot] = {}

    def declare(self, name: str, slot: Slot) -> None:
        self.names[name] = slot

    def lookup(self, name: str) -> Optional[Slot]:
        scope: Optional[_Scope] = self
        while scope is not None:
            if name in scope.names:
                return scope.names[name]
            scope = scope.parent
        return None


class _Lowerer:
    def __init__(self, ast: dict, callee_types: dict[str, str]):
        self.ast = ast
        self.callee_types = callee_types
        self.functions: list[Function] = []
        # Per-function state, reset in _lower_function.
        self.blocks: list[Block] = []
        self.local_slots: list[Slot] = []
        self.current: Optional[Block] = None
        self._block_id = 0
        self._temp_id = 0
        self._slot_id = 0

    # -- generic construction helpers -------------------------------------

    def new_block(self) -> Block:
        block = Block(self._block_id)
        self._block_id += 1
        self.blocks.append(block)
        return block

    def new_temp(self, typ: str) -> Temp:
        temp = Temp(self._temp_id, typ)
        self._temp_id += 1
        return temp

    def new_slot(self, typ: str) -> Slot:
        slot = Slot(self._slot_id, typ)
        self._slot_id += 1
        return slot

    def emit(self, instruction) -> None:
        if self.current is not None and not self.current.is_terminated:
            self.current.instructions.append(instruction)

    def terminate(self, terminator) -> None:
        if self.current is not None:
            self.current.terminator = terminator
            self.current = None

    # -- module / functions ------------------------------------------------

    def lower(self) -> Module:
        for func in self.ast["functions"]:
            self.functions.append(self._lower_function(func))
        return Module(self.functions)

    def _lower_function(self, func: dict) -> Function:
        self.blocks = []
        self.local_slots = []
        self.current = None
        self._block_id = 0
        self._temp_id = 0
        self._slot_id = 0

        scope = _Scope(None)
        params: list[Parameter] = []
        for param in func["params"]:
            slot = self.new_slot(param["type"])
            scope.declare(param["name"], slot)
            params.append(Parameter(param["name"], slot))

        entry = self.new_block()
        self.current = entry

        self._ret_type = func["ret_type"]
        self.lower_stmts(func["body"], scope)

        if self.current is not None:
            # Reachable fall-through is only possible for a void function;
            # the semantic pass guarantees non-void functions return on
            # every reachable path.
            self.current.terminator = Return(None)
            self.current = None

        return Function(
            func["name"],
            params,
            func["ret_type"],
            list(self.local_slots),
            self.blocks,
            entry,
        )

    # -- statements --------------------------------------------------------

    def lower_stmts(self, stmts: list, scope: _Scope) -> None:
        for stmt in stmts:
            if self.current is None:
                # A terminator already ended this path; later statements on
                # the same path produce no IR.
                return
            self.lower_stmt(stmt, scope)

    def lower_stmt(self, stmt: dict, scope: _Scope) -> None:
        kind = stmt["kind"]
        if kind == "let":
            value = self.lower_expr(stmt["init"], scope)
            slot = self.new_slot(stmt["type"])
            self.local_slots.append(slot)
            # The name is bound only after the initializer has been lowered.
            scope.declare(stmt["name"], slot)
            self.emit(Copy(slot, value))
            return
        if kind == "assign":
            value = self.lower_expr(stmt["value"], scope)
            slot = scope.lookup(stmt["target"])
            # Semantic analysis already proved this is bound.
            self.emit(Copy(slot, value))
            return
        if kind == "if":
            self._lower_if(stmt, scope)
            return
        if kind == "while":
            self._lower_while(stmt, scope)
            return
        if kind == "return":
            value = None
            if stmt["value"] is not None:
                value = self.lower_expr(stmt["value"], scope)
            self.terminate(Return(value))
            return
        # block
        self.lower_stmts(stmt["body"], _Scope(scope))

    def _lower_if(self, stmt: dict, scope: _Scope) -> None:
        cond = self.lower_expr(stmt["cond"], scope)
        # Blocks are created in DFS visitation order: true, false, merge.
        true_block = self.new_block()
        false_block = self.new_block()
        self.terminate(Branch(cond, true_block, false_block))

        self.current = true_block
        self.lower_stmts(stmt["then"], _Scope(scope))
        true_end = self.current

        self.current = false_block
        self.lower_stmts(stmt["else"], _Scope(scope))
        false_end = self.current

        if true_end is None and false_end is None:
            # Both branches return: there is no continuation, so no merge
            # block is created at all.
            return

        merge = self.new_block()
        if true_end is not None:
            true_end.terminator = Jump(merge)
        if false_end is not None:
            false_end.terminator = Jump(merge)
        self.current = merge

    def _lower_while(self, stmt: dict, scope: _Scope) -> None:
        cond_block = self.new_block()
        self.terminate(Jump(cond_block))

        self.current = cond_block
        cond = self.lower_expr(stmt["cond"], scope)
        body_block = self.new_block()
        exit_block = self.new_block()
        # A short-circuit condition terminates ``cond_block`` itself and
        # delivers its value in a later merge block; attach the loop branch
        # wherever evaluation actually ends, not blindly to cond_block.
        self.terminate(Branch(cond, body_block, exit_block))

        self.current = body_block
        self.lower_stmts(stmt["body"], _Scope(scope))
        body_end = self.current
        if body_end is not None:
            body_end.terminator = Jump(cond_block)
        # If the body always returns, the back edge simply does not exist;
        # the exit block remains reachable from the condition check.

        self.current = exit_block

    # -- expressions -------------------------------------------------------

    def lower_expr(self, expr: dict, scope: _Scope):
        """Return the value reference (Temp or Slot) holding the result."""
        kind = expr["kind"]
        if kind == "int":
            temp = self.new_temp(INT)
            self.emit(Const(temp, int(expr["value"])))
            return temp
        if kind == "bool":
            temp = self.new_temp(BOOL)
            self.emit(Const(temp, bool(expr["value"])))
            return temp
        if kind == "var":
            return scope.lookup(expr["name"])
        if kind == "arith":
            left = self.lower_expr(expr["left"], scope)
            right = self.lower_expr(expr["right"], scope)
            temp = self.new_temp(INT)
            self.emit(BinOp(temp, expr["op"], left, right, "arith", INT))
            return temp
        if kind == "compare":
            left = self.lower_expr(expr["left"], scope)
            right = self.lower_expr(expr["right"], scope)
            temp = self.new_temp(BOOL)
            self.emit(BinOp(temp, expr["op"], left, right, "compare", BOOL))
            return temp
        if kind == "logical":
            return self._lower_logical(expr, scope)
        # call
        args = [self.lower_expr(arg, scope) for arg in expr["args"]]
        ret_type = self.callee_types[expr["name"]]
        temp = self.new_temp(ret_type)
        self.emit(Call(temp, expr["name"], args, ret_type))
        return temp

    def _lower_logical(self, expr: dict, scope: _Scope) -> Temp:
        op = expr["op"]
        left = self.lower_expr(expr["left"], scope)

        # Blocks are created in DFS visitation order: true, false, merge.
        true_block = self.new_block()
        false_block = self.new_block()
        merge_block = self.new_block()
        self.terminate(Branch(left, true_block, false_block))

        # ``and`` evaluates the right operand on the true path and folds to
        # false on the false path; ``or`` mirrors that.
        rhs_on_true_path = op == "and"
        short_value = not rhs_on_true_path  # False for and, True for or

        result: Optional[Temp] = None

        def visit(block: Block, evaluates_rhs: bool) -> None:
            nonlocal result
            self.current = block
            if evaluates_rhs:
                right = self.lower_expr(expr["right"], scope)
                # The right operand may itself branch (nested short
                # circuit); the copy belongs to whatever block it ends in,
                # not necessarily to ``block``.
                end = self.current
                if result is None:
                    result = self.new_temp(BOOL)
                end.instructions.append(Copy(result, right))
                end.terminator = Jump(merge_block)
                self.current = None
            else:
                if result is None:
                    result = self.new_temp(BOOL)
                self.emit(Const(result, short_value))
                block.terminator = Jump(merge_block)
                self.current = None

        visit(true_block, rhs_on_true_path)
        visit(false_block, not rhs_on_true_path)

        self.current = merge_block
        assert result is not None
        return result


def lower_module(ast: dict) -> Module:
    """Validate, analyze and lower a plain-data program AST to a Module."""
    validate_program(ast)
    analyze(ast)
    callee_types = {func["name"]: func["ret_type"] for func in ast["functions"]}
    return _Lowerer(ast, callee_types).lower()


# Public alias.
lower_ir = lower_module

"""Pass-ordering and idempotency regression tests for the optimizer.

Nothing here adds a language feature or touches the public entry points,
the default pipeline, the diagnostics or the emitted text format; this
module only *observes* the existing pipeline from more angles.

The pipeline under test maps the spec vocabulary onto this repository as
follows:

* front end (type checking + AST -> IR lowering): :func:`lower_module`;
* SSA construction: :func:`to_ssa`;
* SSA optimization: :func:`eliminate_dead_code` (the only IR-level
  optimization pass; constant folding/propagation do not exist here, so
  the repeatability checks target the passes that do);
* final emission ("target code"): :func:`render_module`, the fixed last
  stage of every ordering -- no variant moves a pass after it.

Legal orderings
---------------
A pass ordering is legal when it honours the existing stage constraints:
SSA construction precedes the SSA-dependent DCE pass, and rendering stays
last.  Within those constraints this suite exercises the default order
``lower -> ssa -> dce -> render`` plus the legal variants ``ssa``,
``ssa+dce+dce``, ``ssa+ssa+dce`` and ``ssa+dce+ssa+dce`` (both ``to_ssa``
and ``eliminate_dead_code`` accept their own output again).

What is compared
----------------
* Same source + same order, compiled repeatedly (in-process, across
  processes and across hash seeds): the emitted text must be
  byte-identical.
* Across *different* legal orders only observable semantics must agree --
  the return value, the ordered call trace (this language has no stdout;
  the call trace is its observable output channel) and, for the defined
  runtime error of the language (division/modulus by zero), the error
  category and the trap location ``(function, block)``.  Textual or
  structural equality across orders is never used as a correctness
  criterion, and one test pins that the orders genuinely differ in text.
* Idempotency: applying ``to_ssa`` / ``eliminate_dead_code`` (or the whole
  default sequence) to their own result changes neither the normalized IR
  text nor the final emitted text, and a second DCE performs no new
  structural removals.
* The unoptimized (lower-only) module is the semantic baseline; every
  expected value is also pinned literally so the baseline itself is
  anchored.  All programs are fully defined -- no undefined-behaviour
  sample takes part in the semantic comparison.

Every failure message names the source sample, the pass order and the
first divergent observable result.  All inputs are fixed; nothing uses
randomness, wall-clock time or hash-order-dependent iteration.
"""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

from compiler_ir import (
    BinOp,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
    TypeCheckError,
    UndefinedSymbolError,
    eliminate_dead_code,
    lower_module,
    render_module,
    to_ssa,
)

from test_pipeline import (
    arith,
    assign,
    bool_,
    call,
    compare,
    func,
    if_,
    int_,
    let,
    param,
    program,
    ret,
    var,
    while_,
)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# IR interpreter with defined runtime errors
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Mirrors the interpreter in test_semantic_equivalence.py but covers the
# full arithmetic operator set of the language (add/sub/mul/div/mod) and
# reports the language's defined runtime error -- division or modulus by
# zero -- as a _Trap carrying its category and source location.


_STEP_LIMIT = 100_000

_ARITH = {
    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
}

_COMPARE = {
    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}

Confirmed: `_clone_ssa_function` renumbers SSA values densely (`next_id` from 0), so feeding a DCE'd module (with numbering holes) back through `to_ssa` *renormalizes* the numbering. This is existing, documented behavior ("copies it to an equivalent SSA module with no new phi nodes and unchanged numbering" — the README claim of "unchanged numbering" applies to to_ssa output, which is already dense; DCE output has holes, and re-SSA compacts them).

So my test expectation was wrong, not the compiler: re-applying the full sequence `ssa+dce` to a DCE'd result is NOT textually stable at the `to_ssa` step because re-SSA renumbers. The pipeline's actual idempotency properties are:

- `to_ssa(to_ssa(x))` ≡ `to_ssa(x)` — idempotent on dense SSA (my test_ssa_conversion_is_idempotent passes).
- `dce(dce(x))` ≡ `dce(x)` — idempotent (passes).
- Full sequence re-application: `dce(to_ssa(dce(to_ssa(x))))` — the re-SSA renumbers, then DCE... the result is textually *different* from `dce(to_ssa(x))` only in numbering compaction? Wait — is it? After re-SSA renumbers densely and DCE removes nothing more, the result has dense numbering, whereas the first-pass result has holes. So text differs (numbering only). But is a *second* re-application stable? `dce(to_ssa(y))` where y already dense → to_ssa preserves numbering (dense→same dense), dce no-op → stable. So the fixpoint is reached after one renormalization.

How to handle this in the test while respecting "对该结果再次应用同一序列，规范化IR和最终目标代码都不得继续变化"? The honest approach: the idempotency claim must match the actual pass semantics. The re-SSA renumbering is a *normalization* — the spec says "规范化IR...不得继续变化" (the normalized IR must not keep changing). Since re-SSA is itself the normalizer, the correct fixed-point assertion is: applying the sequence to the *normalized* result is stable. I.e., let `normalized = to_ssa(optimized)` (renumbered), then `dce(to_ssa(normalized))` renders identically to `normalized`... wait, dce(normalized) — normalized is dense with no dead code, so dce is a no-op clone → render equal. And to_ssa(normalized) = normalized. So the stable assertion: once normalized, the sequence doesn't change anything.

So restructure the test:
1. `optimized = dce(to_ssa(lower))`.
2. `normalized = to_ssa(optimized)` — one renormalization step (may compact numbering holes left by DCE).
3. Assert `render(dce(to_ssa(normalized))) == render(normalized)` — the full sequence is a fixed point on the normalized IR.
4. Also assert `render(to_ssa(normalized)) == render(normalized)` and dce no-op — covered by other tests but fine.

Also assert that renormalization is semantics-preserving (already covered by cross-order semantics test which includes "ssa+dce+ssa+dce" order).

Also should I assert that the only difference between optimized and normalized is numbering? That's structural; simpler to just assert the fixed point. And importantly: `render(dce(to_ssa(optimized)))` should equal `render(normalized)` when normalized has no dead code — i.e. `dce(to_ssa(optimized))` == `to_ssa(optimized)` textually (DCE after renormalization removes nothing). That's a good idempotency statement: after one full sequence + renormalization, further applications don't change anything.

## 规格到本仓库的映射

该仓库的实际管线是 `lower_module`（类型检查 + AST→IR 降低）→ `to_ssa`（SSA 构造）→ `eliminate_dead_code`（唯一的 SSA 优化遍）→ `render_module`（最终发射阶段，所有顺序中都位于最后）。仓库没有常量折叠/传播/内联遍，也没有 stdout——测试只观察真实存在的遍，call trace 作为可观察输出通道，除零（`div`/`mod` 是语言定义的运算符）作为语言已定义的运行时错误。

## 覆盖内容

**测试程序**（7 个，全部行为已定义，固定输入、无随机性）：分支汇合处的常量与 Phi、可删除纯计算与有副作用调用并存、含循环不变量与循环内分支的循环、可内联形态的调用及调用后死代码、入口块除零陷阱、受保护路径上的除法（不触发）、分支块内陷阱（检验非入口块 `b1` 的触发位置）。

**跨顺序语义等价**：默认顺序 `ssa+dce` 加 4 个满足前置条件的变体（`ssa`、`ssa+dce+dce`、`ssa+ssa+dce`、`ssa+dce+ssa+dce`），每个都与未优化（仅 lower）基准比较返回值、调用 trace、以及陷阱时的错误类别和触发位置 `(函数, 基本块)`；基准值另有字面值锚定。失败信息包含源码样例名、遍顺序、首个分歧的可观察结果和可复现 AST。

**字节一致**：同一源码 + 同一顺序连续编译 3 次逐字节一致；另用子进程在 `PYTHONHASHSEED=0/1` 下验证默认管线跨进程字节一致。

**幂等性**：`to_ssa`、`eliminate_dead_code` 各自幂等（文本 + 定义数不变）；完整序列在再规范化结果上是不动点。

**不以文本相等为判据**：显式断言 `ssa` 与 `ssa+dce` 文本不同但语义一致。

**阶段约束与诊断**：`dce` 跳过 `ssa` 必须抛 `ValueError`；类型错误/未定义符号在所有顺序下抛出相同错误类型。
